Surah 55: Ar-Rahman (The Most Merciful)

Makki (revealed in Makkah). [Al-Nahhas reported from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that Surah al-Rahman was revealed in Makkah. Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: Surah al-Rahman was revealed in Makkah. Ibn Mardawayh also reported from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with them both) who said: Surah al-Rahman was revealed in Makkah. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/689; al-Qurtubi: 17/151.]] ﷽

* *

﴿The Most Merciful﴾. It is said: it was revealed when they said: "And what is the Most Merciful?" [See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/187-188.] It is also said: it is a reply to the people of Makkah when they said: "It is only a human who teaches him."

﴿Taught the Qur'an﴾. Al-Kalbi said: He taught Muhammad the Qur'an. It is also said: "Taught the Qur'an" means He made it easy to remember.

﴿Created man﴾, meaning Adam (peace be upon him), as said by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah.

﴿Taught him eloquent speech (al-bayan)﴾: the names of everything. It is also said: He taught him all languages, and Adam spoke seven hundred [thousand] languages, the best of which was Arabic.

Others said: "al-insan" is a generic noun and by it he meant all people. "Taught him al-bayan": speech, writing, understanding and making understood, until he knew what he was saying and what was said to him. This is the saying of Abu al-Aliyah, Ibn Zayd and al-Hasan.

Al-Suddi said: He taught each people the tongue they speak.

Ibn Kaysan said: "Created man" means Muhammad (ﷺ), "taught him al-bayan" means the explanation of what has been and what will be, for he used to clarify (for) the former and latter peoples and about the Day of Religion.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 55, verses 5–11:**

﴿The sun and the moon [run] by calculation.﴾ Mujahid said: "Like the millstone's [revolving] wheel (*ḥusbān al-raḥā*)." Others said: that is, they run according to a reckoning and to stations that they do not exceed. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan said: by them time and terms are reckoned. Were it not for the night, the day, the sun, and the moon, no one would know how to calculate anything. Al-Dahhak said: they run by decree. *Al-ḥusbān* can be the verbal noun of *ḥasibtu ḥisāban wa ḥusbānan* (I reckoned), like *al-ghufrān* and *al-kufrān*, and *al-rujḥān* and *al-nuqṣān*. It can also be the plural of *al-ḥisāb*, like *al-shubhān* and *al-rukbān*.

﴿And the star and the tree prostrate.﴾ *Al-najm* is what has no stalk of plants, and *al-shajar* is what has a stalk that remains through the winter. Their prostration is the prostration of their shadows, as He said: ﴿Whose shadows incline from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 48]. Mujahid said: *al-najm* is the star, and its prostration is its rising.

﴿And the heaven He raised,﴾ above the earth, ﴿and He set up the balance,﴾ Mujahid said: by the balance he meant justice. The meaning is that He commanded justice, as indicated by His saying: ﴿that you not transgress in the balance﴾, that is, that you not exceed justice. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: it means the instrument by which things are weighed, so that by it fairness and redress are achieved. The root of *al-wazn* (weighing) is measuring. ﴿That you not transgress﴾ means: lest you deviate, wrong others, and exceed the right in the balance.

﴿And establish the weight with justice,﴾ with equity. Abu al-Darda' and Ata' said: its meaning is, "Set the tongue of the balance straight with justice." Ibn Uyaynah said: the setting straight is by the hand, and the justice is by the heart. ﴿And do not make deficient﴾, and do not diminish ﴿the balance﴾, and do not give short measure in measuring and weighing.

﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures,﴾ for the creation that He spread upon it.

﴿In it is fruit,﴾ meaning: kinds of fruits. Ibn Kaysan said: meaning what they enjoy of innumerable blessings. ﴿And the palm tree, having sheaths,﴾ *al-akmām* are the containers in which the fruit is, because the fruit of the palm is within a covering until it splits open. Its singular is *kimm*, and everything that covers something is a *kimm* and *kimmah*; from it comes *kumm al-qamīṣ* (the sleeve of the shirt), and a skullcap is called *kummah*. Al-Dahhak said: "having sheaths" means having coverings. Al-Hasan said: its *akmām* are its spathes. [Ibn Zayd said: it is the spathe before it splits open.] [[The text between the brackets is missing from "a".]]

﴿And the star and the tree prostrate.﴾ *Al-najm* is what has no stalk of plants, and *al-shajar* is what has a stalk that remains through the winter. Their prostration is the prostration of their shadows, as He said: ﴿Whose shadows incline from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 48]. Mujahid said: *al-najm* is the star, and its prostration is its rising.

﴿And the heaven He raised,﴾ above the earth, ﴿and He set up the balance,﴾ Mujahid said: by the balance he meant justice. The meaning is that He commanded justice, as indicated by His saying: ﴿that you not transgress in the balance﴾, that is, that you not exceed justice. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: it means the instrument by which things are weighed, so that by it fairness and redress are achieved. The root of *al-wazn* (weighing) is measuring. ﴿That you not transgress﴾ means: lest you deviate, wrong others, and exceed the right in the balance.

﴿And establish the weight with justice,﴾ with equity. Abu al-Darda' and Ata' said: its meaning is, "Set the tongue of the balance straight with justice." Ibn Uyaynah said: the setting straight is by the hand, and the justice is by the heart. ﴿And do not make deficient﴾, and do not diminish ﴿the balance﴾, and do not give short measure in measuring and weighing.

﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures,﴾ for the creation that He spread upon it.

﴿In it is fruit,﴾ meaning: kinds of fruits. Ibn Kaysan said: meaning what they enjoy of innumerable blessings. ﴿And the palm tree, having sheaths,﴾ *al-akmām* are the containers in which the fruit is, because the fruit of the palm is within a covering until it splits open. Its singular is *kimm*, and everything that covers something is a *kimm* and *kimmah*; from it comes *kumm al-qamīṣ* (the sleeve of the shirt), and a skullcap is called *kummah*. Al-Dahhak said: "having sheaths" means having coverings. Al-Hasan said: its *akmām* are its spathes. [Ibn Zayd said: it is the spathe before it splits open.] [[The text between the brackets is missing from "a".]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 55, verses 12–13:

﴿And the grain, with its husk, and the fragrant plant.﴾ He meant by "the grain" all the grains that are sown in the earth. Mujahid said: it is the leaves of the crop.

Ibn Kaysan said: "al-'asf (the husk) is the leaf of everything from which the grain emerges. It first appears as a leaf, which is the 'asf, then it becomes a stalk (suq), then Allah brings forth sheaths (akmam) in it, then He brings forth the grain within the sheaths."

Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of al-Walibi, said: it is the chaff (tibn). This is also the view of al-Dahhak and Qatadah. 'Atiyyah reported from him: it is the leaves of the green crop when its heads have been cut off and it has dried out. A parallel is His saying: ﴿like a field eaten up﴾ [al-Fil: 5].

﴿And the fragrant plant﴾: according to most scholars, it is provision (rizq). Ibn 'Abbas said: every "rayhan" in the Qur'an means provision. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: it is your fragrant plant that is smelled. Al-Dahhak said: "al-'asf" is the chaff, and "al-rayhan" is its fruit.

The reading of the majority is: "wal-habbu dhu al-'asfi wal-rayhanu," all of them in the nominative, by way of coordination with "al-fakihah" (the fruit). Ibn 'Amir read "wal-habba dhal-'asfi war-rayhana," with the ba' and the nun in the accusative and "dha" with an alif, meaning: He created man and He created these things. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "wal-rayhani" in the genitive, coordinating it with "al-'asf," so He mentioned the sustenance of people and of livestock. Then He addressed the jinn and mankind, saying:

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ O you two weighty ones (al-thaqalan), meaning from these things that have been mentioned. He repeated this verse in this surah to affirm the blessing and to emphasise the reminder of it, in keeping with the Arab custom of emphasis and thoroughness. He enumerates His favours upon creation and separates every two blessings with something that draws their attention to them, like the saying of a man to one who has done him good and followed up his bounties upon him while he denies and disbelieves them: "Were you not poor and did I not enrich you? Will you deny this? Were you not naked and did I not clothe you? Will you deny this? Were you not obscure and did I not honour you? Will you deny this?" Such repetition is common in Arabic speech and is good for affirmation.

It has also been said: He addressed them using the dual form, according to the Arab custom of addressing one person with the dual form, as in His saying: ﴿Cast into Hell﴾ [Qaf: 24].

It is narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to us Surah al-Rahman until he finished it, then said: "What is wrong with me, that I see you silent? The jinn were better than you in response. Whenever I recited to them this verse, 'So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?' they would say: 'Nor of any of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny. To You be praise.'"

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 55, verses 14–21:

﴿He created man from clay like pottery.﴾ .

﴿And He created the jinn﴾, and he is the father of the jinn. Al-Dahhak said: he is Iblis. ﴿from a smokeless flame of fire﴾, which is the pure part of the blaze of fire that has no smoke in it. Mujahid said: it is what is mixed, one part with another, of the red, yellow and green flame that rises above the fire when it is kindled, from their saying: "the affair of the people became confused (maraja)", when it became mixed.

﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny? Lord of the two easts﴾: the east of summer and the east of winter.

﴿And Lord of the two wests﴾: the west of summer and the west of winter.

﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ .

﴿He released the two seas﴾: the sweet and the salty. He let them go and left them ﴿to meet﴾ .

﴿Between them is a barrier﴾: a barrier from the power of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿they do not transgress﴾: they do not mix, they do not change, and neither of them oppresses the other. Qatadah said: they do not rise up against the people with drowning. Al-Hasan said: "He released the two seas" refers to the Sea of Rum and the Sea of India, and you are the barrier between them. It is also reported from Qatadah: the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rum, with a barrier between them, meaning the islands. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth, which meet every year. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ .

﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا﴾ [From both of them there comes forth]. The people of Medina and Basra read "يُخْرَجُ" (yukhraju) with a ḍamma on the yā' and a fatḥa on the rā', while the others read it with a fatḥa on the yā' and a ḍamma on the rā'. ﴿اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾ [the pearl and the coral]. Pearls and coral come out only of the salt water, not the sweet water. In the speech of the Arabs it is permissible to mention two things and then attribute an action to only one of them, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ" [Al-An'am: 130] ("O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?"). The messengers were from mankind, not from the jinn. Some of them said: it comes out of the rain water and the sea water. Ibn Jurayj said: when the sky rains, the oyster shells open their mouths, and wherever a drop falls it becomes a pearl. The "lu'lu'ah" (pearl) is the large of the pearls, and the "marjan" is their small ones. Muqatil and Mujahid said the opposite of this. It was also said that "al-marjan" is the red beads. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said it is the "yusr" [[In "A": al-busd.]].

﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?]

﴿وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِي﴾ [And His are the ships] – the large ships. ﴿الْمُنْشَآتُ﴾ [raised up]. Ḥamzah and Abu Bakr read "الْمُنْشِئَاتُ" (al-munshi'at) with a kasra on the shīn, meaning those that set out to sail, i.e., those that began and initiated the voyage [what is between the brackets is an addition from "B"]. The others read it with a fatḥa on the shīn, meaning "al-marfu'at" (those raised up), which are the ships whose timbers are raised one upon another. It was also said: they are the ships whose sails are raised; as for those whose sails are not raised, they are not among the "munshi'at." It was also said: they are the created things that are subjected (to service). ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ﴾ [in the sea like mountains] – like the mountains; "a'lam" is the plural of "'alam," which is a tall mountain. He likened the ships in the sea to the mountains on land. ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?]

﴿كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا﴾ [Everyone upon it] – that is, upon the earth, of living creatures – ﴿فَانٍ﴾ [is passing away], for he is perishing.

﴿وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ﴾ [And there remains the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty] – Owner of greatness and magnificence ﴿وَالْإِكْرَامِ﴾ [and Honour]; that is, He honours His prophets and His friends with His kindness together with His majesty and greatness.

﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?]

﴿يَسْأَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ﴾ [Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks of Him; every day He is upon some matter] (55:29).

﴿يَسْأَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ – of angels, mankind and jinn. Qatadah said: the people of the heavens and the earth cannot do without Him. Ibn 'Abbas said: the people of the heavens ask Him for forgiveness, and the people of the earth ask Him for mercy [and provision, repentance and forgiveness] [what is between the brackets is an addition from "B"]. ﴿يَسْأَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ – of angels, mankind and jinn. Qatadah said: the people of the heavens and the earth cannot do without Him. Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shariḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdus al-Muzakki informed us by dictation; Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Bazzaz informed us; Yahya ibn al-Rabi' al-Makki informed us; Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us; Abu Hamzah al-Thumali informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created is a tablet of white pearl, whose two covers are red ruby; its pen is light and its writing is light. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: The whole of time with God is two days: one of them is the duration of the days of this world, and the other is the Day of Resurrection. So the affair in which He is during the day that is the duration of the world is: informing about the command and prohibition, giving life and causing death, giving and withholding. The affair of the Day of Resurrection is: recompense and reckoning, reward and punishment [[See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/193; al-Qurtubi: 17/166-167.]].

It was also said: His affair, may His remembrance be exalted, is that He brings forth in every day and night three hosts: a host from the loins of fathers into the wombs of mothers, a host from the wombs into this world, and a host from this world into the graves; then they all journey together to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is driving the decrees toward their appointed times [[See Zad al-Masir: 8/114.]]. Abu Sulayman al-Darani said concerning this verse: "Every day has for the servants a new bir [بر جديد] ١٤٨/أ."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 55, verse 30–33:

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ ﴿We shall soon attend to you, O two burdens!﴾ Ḥamzah and al-Kisa'i read "sa-yafrughu" (with the letter yā’), on account of His saying: "Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him" [55:29], "And there remains the Face of your Lord" [55:27], and "And His are the ships" [55:24]; so they followed the preceding report (in the third person).

The others read it with nūn, and the intended meaning is not "freedom from preoccupation," because God, exalted is He, is not occupied by one affair to the exclusion of another. Rather, it is a threat from God Most High to the creation (in "a" it reads "to the creature") with reckoning, like the saying of one who says: "I will surely attend to you," while he has no preoccupation. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Ḍaḥḥak. This "attending" was apt only because the matter ("shaʾn") was mentioned before.

Others said: its meaning is: "We shall turn to you after leaving you alone and granting you respite, and we shall take up your affair," like the saying of one to a person with no occupation: "You have become free for me." Some of them said: God promised the people of piety and threatened the people of wickedness, then He said: "We shall attend to you concerning what We promised you and informed you of," so We will reckon with you, recompense you, and fulfil for you what We promised you; this will be completed and finished. This is the view of al-Ḥasan and Muqatil.

﴿O you two burdens!﴾ That is, the jinn and mankind. They were called "two burdens" (thaqalān) because they are a burden upon the earth, alive and dead. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the earth brings out its burdens﴾ [99:2]. Some scholars of meanings said: everything that has a measure and weight over which people compete is a "thaql" (burden). The Prophet ﷺ said: "I am leaving among you the two burdens: the Book of God and my family (ʿitrah)" [Narrated by Imam Aḥmad: 3/14, 17. See Ṣaḥīḥ al-Jāmiʿ no. (2457).] So he made them "two burdens" in order to magnify their status.

Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq said: the jinn and mankind were called "two burdens" because they are weighed down by sins. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind! If you are able to pass through﴾, that is, to cross over and escape, ﴿the regions of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their sides and extremities, ﴿then pass through﴾. The meaning is: if you are able to flee from death by going out of the regions of the heavens and the earth, then flee and go out from them. [And the meaning is] — (omitted in "a") — wherever you are, death will overtake you, as He, majestic is His remembrance, said: "Wherever you may be, death will overtake you" [4:78]. It was also said: it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection: "If you are able to cross the extremities of the heavens and the earth, and so overcome your Lord so that He cannot prevail over you, then cross over." ﴿You will not pass through except with authority﴾, that is, with dominion; and it was said, with proof. Authority (sulṭān) is the power by which one gains control over a matter, so dominion, power and proof are all sulṭān. The meaning is: wherever you turn, you are within My dominion and My authority. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: its meaning is: "If you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know; and you will not know it except with authority," that is, with a clear proof from God, mighty and majestic. [Narrated by al-Ṭabarī: 27/137. Mentioned by al-Qurṭubī: 17/170.] It was also said that His saying "except with authority" means "except toward authority," like His saying: "And He was indeed good to me" [12:100], meaning "to me."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 55, verses 34–35:

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ And in a report: the creation will be surrounded by angels, and with a tongue of fire, and then they will be called: ﴿O company of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority.﴾ This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿A flame of fire will be sent against you both﴾.

﴿A flame of fire will be sent against you both﴾. Ibn Kathir read "shuwaz" with a kasra on the shin, while the others read it with a damma. Both are dialectal forms (lughatan), like "ṣiwar" and "ṣuwar" for a herd of cows. It is the blazing flame without smoke; this is the view of most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: it is the green flame that is cut off from the fire.

﴿And smoke﴾. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "wa-nuhasin" with a kasra on the sin, as a conjunction with "al-nar" (fire). The rest read it with a damma, as a conjunction with "al-shuwaz" (flame).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Kalbi said: "al-nuhas" is smoke, and this is the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas.

The meaning of the damma reading is: a flame will be sent against you, and smoke will be sent; that is, this one at one time and that one at another time. It is also permissible that both are sent together without one mixing with the other. Whoever reads with a kasra by conjunction to "al-nar" is weaker, because there is no "shuwaz" made of copper (nuhas). It is permissible that the implied meaning is: a flame of fire and some copper (shay' min nuhas). It is also reported that a flame does not come from fire and smoke together.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: "al-nuhas" is molten brass (al-sufr al-mudhab) poured over their heads, and this is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: it is al-muhl (molten metal dregs).

﴿So you will not be able to defend yourselves﴾, that is, you will not be able to resist God, and you will have no helper against Him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 55, verse 36–39:

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you two deny?﴾ ﴿And when the sky is split open,﴾ [it becomes spread apart] [[Addition from "B".]] ﴿the sky,﴾ and it becomes gates for the descent of the angels. ﴿And it will be rose-colored like red leather.﴾ That is, like the color of a rose-colored horse, which is white tending toward red and yellow. Qatadah said: "It is green today, and on that Day it will have another color tending toward red."

﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you two deny?﴾ (40)

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 55, verses 41–45:**

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks,﴾ and that is the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes, as the Exalted One said: "On the Day when some faces will be whitened and some faces will be blackened" (Al 'Imran 3:106). ﴿So they will be seized by their forelocks and their feet.﴾ Their feet will be bound to their forelocks from behind, and they will be cast into the Fire. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals (the polytheists) [148b] used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go about between it and scalding water, intensely hot.﴾ Its heat has reached its peak. Al-Zajjaj said: "Ana yani'a" means "he is āni" when he has reached the peak of ripeness. The meaning is that they will run between the blazing Fire and the scalding water. When they cry out for relief from the heat of the Fire, their punishment will be the scalding water that has reached its peak and has become like molten metal (muhl). This is His saying: "And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal" (al-Kahf 18:29). Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Ān" is a valley among the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire gathers. They will be taken to it in shackles and immersed in that valley until their joints come apart. Then they will come out of it, and God, exalted is He, will have created for them a new creation, and they will be cast back into the Fire. (See: al-Qurtubi, 17/175–176.) This is His saying: "They will go about between it and scalding water, intensely hot."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ Everything that God, exalted is He, has mentioned from His saying "Everyone upon it is perishing" up to this point is admonition, warning and intimidation. All of that is a favour from God, exalted is He, because it restrains from sins. For this reason He concluded every verse with His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 55, verses 53–56:**

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿Reclining on furnishings﴾: *furush* is the plural of *firash* (bedding, couch).

﴿Their linings﴾: *bata'in* is the plural of *bitana*, which is what lies beneath the *zihara* (the outer layer). Al-Zajjaj said: they are the parts that face the ground.

﴿Of brocade﴾: *istabraq* is what is thick of *dibaj* (silk brocade). Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayra said: these are the linings, so what do you think of the outer surfaces?[[I have not found this statement attributed to Abu Hurayra; it is rather attributed to Hubayra, as mentioned by al-Tabari: 27/149, or on the authority of Hubayra ibn Maryam from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, as mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/278.]] It was said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The linings are of brocade, so what are the outer surfaces?" He said: "This is among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajda: 17].[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 27/149. See also: al-Qurtubi: 17/179.]] And from him also, he said: their linings are of brocade, and their outer surfaces are of solid light.[[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/710 to Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya.]] Ibn Abbas said: He described the linings and left out the outer surfaces, because there is no one on earth who knows what the outer surfaces are.[[See: al-Qurtubi: 17/179.]]

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near﴾: *al-janan* is what is gathered of fruits; the meaning is that its fruit is near and close, reachable by one standing, sitting, or lying down. Ibn Abbas said: the tree draws near until the friend of Allah picks from it, standing if he wishes, or sitting if he wishes.[[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/197.]] Qatada said: neither distance nor thorns keep their hands from it.

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿Therein are those restraining their gaze﴾: lowering their eyes. They have restricted their gaze to their husbands, not looking at anyone else, and not desiring anyone other than them. Ibn Zayd said: she says to her husband, "By the might of my Lord, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you. All praise is due to Allah who made you my husband and made me your wife."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 27/150.]]

﴿No man or jinn has touched them before﴾: no one has had intercourse with them, and none has taken their virginity.[[Al-iftira': removing the hymen.]] Its root is from *al-tamth*, which is blood, and from it the menstruating woman is called *tamith*. It is as if He said: no one has made them bleed through intercourse. Al-Zajjaj said: In this there is evidence that the jinn may cover [a woman] just as a human does. Mujahid said: When a man has intercourse and does not mention the name of Allah, the jinni coils around his male organ and has intercourse with it.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 27/151. Al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/711 adds that it is attributed to al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul.]]

Muqatil said, concerning His words ﴿No man or jinn has touched them before﴾: because they were created in Paradise. According to his view, these are the *hur* (maidens) of Paradise.

Al-Sha'bi said: They are women of the worldly life, who have not been touched since they were created. This is also the view of al-Kalbi.[[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/711 to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azama.]] That is, no man or jinn has had intercourse with them in this creation in which they were brought into being.

Talha ibn Musarrif read: *la yatmuthhunna* with a *damma* on the *mim* in both places.

Al-Kisa'i read one of the two with a *damma*: if he read the first with a *kasra*, he read the second with a *damma*, and if he read the first with a *damma*, he read the second with a *kasra*. This is based on what Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i narrated, who said: "I used to pray behind the companions of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and I heard them reading *lam yatmuthhunna* with a *raf'* [damma], and I used to pray behind the companions of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and I heard them reading with a *kasra* on the *mim*." Al-Kisa'i would put a *damma* on one and a *kasra* on the other, so as not to depart from these two reports.[[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 3/119.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 55, verses 59–60:**

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you two deny? Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?﴾ That is, the reward of one who does good in this world is nothing but that good will be done to him in the Hereafter. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Is the reward of one who says: there is no god but Allah, and acts upon what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, anything but Paradise?" [[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/714) as narrated by 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh. See also al-Qurtubi (17/182).]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; Ibn Fanjawayh informed me; Ibn Shayba informed us [[In manuscript "A" it reads "Abu Shayba," but the correct reading is what we have written, from manuscript "B." Al-Dhahabi said in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (17/384), in the biography of Ibn Fanjawayh: "Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi narrated from him in the Tafsir, and the memorizer Abu al-Fadl al-Falaki spoke against him, saying: 'He did not hear from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Shayba.' **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 55, verses 63–76:**

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ *Mudhammatan* (dark green), *na'imatan* (lush), *sawda'an* (black), from their greenness and the intensity of their verdure, because when green intensifies it inclines toward black. It is said: *idhdhamma al-zar'u* (the crops turned dark) when blackness overspread them, *riyyan idhdhimamman*, so it is *mudhammam*.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? In them are two springs gushing forth.﴾ *Fawwaratan bil-ma'* (welling up with water), never ceasing. *Al-nadh*' (the gushing) is the welling up of water from the spring. Ibn 'Abbas said: they gush forth with goodness and blessing upon the people of Paradise [[See: al-Tabari: 27/157; al-Qurtubi: 17/185.]]. Ibn Mas'ud said: they gush forth with musk and camphor upon the friends of Allah [[See: al-Qurtubi: 17/185.]]. Anas ibn Malik said: they gush forth with musk and ambergris in the houses of the people of Paradise, like the spraying of rain [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/716 to Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn Abi Hatim. See also: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/198; al-Qurtubi: 17/185.]].

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? In them are fruit, date palms and pomegranates.﴾ Some said: the date palm and the pomegranate are not among the fruits, whereas the general view is that they are fruits. Rather, the mention of the date palm and pomegranate, though they are among the fruits, is repeated for specification and detail [[al-Farra': Ma'ani al-Qur'an: 3/119.]], as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il﴾ [al-Baqarah: 98].

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (69) In them are good and beautiful [women] (70). So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (71) Chaste, secluded maidens in pavilions (72). So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? (73) Untouched before them by any human or jinn (74).
